main_body: Tall Victorian townhouse: slate mansard roof with a flat top, a dormer and a chimney, an orange cornice, then a three-storey brick facade with a balcony and a green door.
top_band: Rows 17-23 at x=24: a light slate-grey roof top (L~95) with a lighter edge line at row 23 (L=122). This is a thin band, but it sits above the sloped slate roof surface.
evidence: Reading down x=24: an outline at row 16, the flat roof top at rows 17-22 and a light edge line at row 23. A dark eave row at 24 follows, then the sloped mansard slate and dormer, the orange cornice at rows 44-45, and the brick wall below. The roof surfaces (flat top plus mansard slope) are drawn as visible surfaces above the facade. The windows have stone surrounds and sills, and the balcony projects, so the front is not painted flat. The wall is a front face, but the roof reads correctly as a surface seen from above.

style.evidence: The brick, slate and stone each have several steps and some texture, with 14 colours per tile against 11-18 for the references. But 90% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7-9% in the references, so the outline is the near-black sticker line rather than the dark tone of the adjacent material. It has only 49 distinct colours against 66 and 185. The slate and brick have less per-unit variation than the reference tiles. A careful artist would see it as thinner and more sticker-like than the references.
